description: List files in the session workspace (VFS). Use it to discover what an `execute` run wrote to disk before reading with `submilli__files__read`. Args: optional `path` (directory, default the working directory) and `recursive` (default false). Returns { entries: [{ path, kind, bytes }], count, truncated }, capped at 1000 entries. Files survive across calls under a per_session or named root and under a mounted volume; an ephemeral root is emptied after every execute. Requires fs.list as caller main with op list; policy checks the starting directory, including recursive listings. A denial or a missing directory returns { error: { kind, message } }.

path.description: Directory to list, e.g. `"/workspace"`. Defaults to the workspace root.

recursive.description: Recurse into subdirectories. Defaults to false (top level only).

name: submilli__files__list

description: Read a file from the session workspace (VFS) in line windows — the smart way to consume a large payload an `execute` run wrote to disk (e.g. via jina `downloadSearch`/`downloadRead`) without pulling it back through a single huge result. Args: `path`, optional `offset` (1-based line, default 1) and `limit` (lines, default 2000). Returns { content, line_start, line_end, has_more, next_offset, bytes }; pass `next_offset` back to page on. Files survive across calls under a per_session or named root and under a mounted volume; an ephemeral root is emptied after every execute. Requires fs.read as caller main with op readText. A denial or a missing file returns { error: { kind, message } }.

limit.description: Maximum lines to return (clamped to 5000). Defaults to 2000.

offset.description: 1-based line to start at. Defaults to 1.

path.description:
VFS path to read, e.g. `"/workspace/search.md"`. Resolved under the session
workspace root; `..` segments that escape it are rejected.

name: submilli__files__read

description: Return TypeScript `.d.ts`-style declarations for one or more language built-ins — the globals always in scope without an `import` (e.g. "Array", "Map", "Temporal", "JSON"). Their signatures are a strict subset and differ from Node/TS in places, so fetch the names you intend to use. A dotted member path (e.g. "Temporal.Instant") returns just that member — much smaller than the whole namespace, so prefer it when you know the member you want. Unknown names return an { error } entry rather than failing. A package name asked here returns an { error } naming the package-docs call to make; use that tool for importable modules.

names.description:
Built-in names to look up, e.g. `["Array", "Map", "Temporal"]`. Each
returns its declarations; unknown names come back with an `error` entry.

name: submilli__typescript__builtins__docs

description: List the language built-ins that are always in scope without an `import`, returning { types, namespaces }. Use this to discover names before fetching their declarations. Built-in namespaces such as Temporal and JSON must be used directly, not imported.
name: submilli__typescript__builtins__list

description:
Run a Submilli program: a strict TypeScript subset, compiled to WebAssembly.

Before your first program, call `submilli__typescript__packages__docs` with every package and module you will import, and use those declarations rather than guessing APIs. `submilli__typescript__packages__search` finds packages, and `submilli__typescript__builtins__docs` declares the built-ins.

Programs are synchronous: never `async`, `await` or `Promise`. Every call, a package's included, returns its value directly. Import every function and type you use from its package (`@scope/name`) or standard-library module (`submilli:url`, `submilli:crypto`, `submilli:uuid`). Built-ins need no import: `console`, Array, BigInt, Boolean, Error, ErrorOptions, Map, Number, Object, PermissionDeniedError, QuotaExceededError, RangeError, ReadonlyMap, ReadonlySet, Record, ReferenceError, RegExp, Set, String, SyntaxError, TextDecoder, TextEncoder, TimeoutError, TypeError, URIError, Uint8Array, and the namespaces JSON, Math and Temporal (there is no `Date`).

```ts
import { list_orders, type Order } from "@shop/orders";

function main(): string[] {
    const large: Order[] = [];
    for (let page = 0; ; page++) {
        const orders = list_orders({ page_index: page });
        if (orders.length === 0) break;
        for (const order of orders) {
            if (order.total > 100) large.push(order);
        }
    }
    return large.map((order) => order.id);
}
```

There is no `any`: use the package's types, or `unknown` narrowed with `typeof`, `Array.isArray` or `===`. Every function declaration needs a return type, `main` included: `function main(): string[]`, never `function main()`. `x == null` is a compile error: write `x === null` or `x === undefined`.

Postfix `x!` is a runtime-checked non-null assertion: it
removes `null` and `undefined` from the type and throws `TypeError` for either.
Missing properties, collection misses, and omitted optional parameters use
`undefined`; `null` is distinct. Defaults apply to omission or `undefined`,
never `null`. Optional chains yield `undefined`; `??` handles both values.
`arr[i]` out of range throws `RangeError`; probe with `arr.at(i)`, which
returns `undefined`. A local `let x: T;` must be assigned on every path before
a read unless `T` includes `undefined`; module-level bindings still need an
initializer in that case. Template literals accept `null` and `undefined` and render them
like `String(x)`.
No runtime reflection: of `Object.prototype` only `.toString()` is
available — no `.hasOwnProperty()`. The type system tells you what
fields a value has; narrow optional values with `obj.field !== undefined`.
`"field" in obj` narrows `unknown` or unions distinguished by field presence;
a present optional field can still hold `undefined`.
Dynamic string keys also work with `key in obj`, without narrowing.
Identifiers follow TypeScript — `type`, `from`,
`of`, `as`, and `is` are contextual and may name variables — with one
exception: `namespace` is reserved here, so rename it (`ns`). Reserved
words are fine as object keys (`{ type: "x" }`, read back as
`obj.type`); for keys that aren't valid identifiers, quote them and
index with a string literal (`{ "content-length": 5 }` →
`obj["content-length"]`). Use `Record<string, V>` or `{ [key: string]: V }`
for dynamic `obj[key]` reads and writes. Missing reads return `undefined`, so
their read type is `V | undefined`; writes require `V`. `Record<"a" | "b", V>` requires
both keys and reads them as `V`. Computed literals (`{ [key]: value }`), spread,
and readonly string index signatures are supported. Keys must be strings;
`keyof` an open string-indexed type is `string`. General mapped types and
unresolved generic Record keys are unsupported.

Do the work in one program: follow pagination and data dependencies in code, filter and aggregate there, and return only what the answer or your next decision needs.

The output is what `main()` returns: a string as is, anything else as JSON. `console.log` goes to a separate debug stream, and a failed run returns the error with the console output.

code.description:
TypeScript-subset source with a `main()` entry point. Its return value
is the tool result.

name: submilli__typescript__execute

description: Return the most recent execution's result and FULL console (un-suppressed) for this session. Use it to read debug output after a successful run, which the execute result omits. Takes no arguments.
name: submilli__typescript__last_run

description: Read documentation and TypeScript declarations for `names: string[]` in one call. Before your first program, fetch every module or package you will import; use the returned signatures rather than guessing Node or TypeScript APIs. Returns { results: [{ name, found, text }] } in request order, retaining duplicates. Unknown names have found=false and an explanation in text; other entries still succeed. Accepts stdlib names (e.g. submilli:fs), registry packages, @mcp/<server>, and built-ins (e.g. Temporal, used without an import). A bare stdlib name such as fs resolves when visible and its text identifies the canonical import name submilli:fs.

names.description: Package or built-in names to read before writing the program.

name: submilli__typescript__packages__docs

description: Search available packages by name, description, or exported symbol name — stdlib modules (e.g. "submilli:crypto"), this blueprint's declared registry packages (e.g. "@submilli/github"), and its discovered @mcp/<server> packages (results tagged with a "source" of "host", "registry", or "mcp"). An empty query lists every available package. A query matching nothing returns the available-package catalog and a pointer to the built-ins tool rather than an empty list.

query.description:
Substring matched against module names, descriptions, and exported
symbols. Empty lists every available package.

name: submilli__typescript__packages__search
